experiment: Offline single-server scheduling analysis over measured NLLB FP16 full-prefix translation latencies.
limitations: Service times are reused from mt_10 rather than remeasured in a live asynchronous scheduler.
Desktop RTX 3060 measurements remain development results and must not be treated as final Jetson Orin performance.
The analysis models only the MT worker and does not yet include simultaneous ASR/TTS GPU contention.

methodology.arrival_time: audio_available_s from the stable2_hold1 ASR source commit.
methodology.inference: No new NLLB inference is executed by mt_14.
methodology.latest_only_preemption: No running MT inference is cancelled. Only pending obsolete prefixes are discarded.
methodology.server: One non-preemptive MT worker per utterance-target sequence.
methodology.service_time: Measured total_ms of the corresponding NLLB FP16 full-prefix translation in mt_10.

quality_preservation.final_translation: All schedulers process the same final full source prefix used by mt_10. Therefore the final NLLB translation is preserved exactly.
quality_preservation.note: No claim is made that intermediate target behaviour is identical, because latest_only intentionally skips obsolete intermediate translations.
quality_preservation.principle: Scheduling does not alter the NLLB model, decoding configuration, or source text of a selected translation.

schedulers.every_commit_fifo: Translate every committed ASR prefix in arrival order. This reproduces the mt_10 naive baseline.
schedulers.final_only: Ignore all intermediate ASR commits and translate only the final complete source prefix.
schedulers.latest_only: If MT is busy, retain only the newest pending ASR prefix. Translations already running are allowed to complete.
